ing: half chopped for the marinade, half finely diced for serving
st: Soak the guajillo chiles in hot water for 15 minutes until soft, then drain.
Blend the chiles with the achiote paste, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano, [[2 tsp]] salt, half the onion and [[0.5 cup]] of the pineapple until smooth.
Toss the sliced pork with the marinade in a bowl or zip bag. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or up to overnight.
Heat a large skillet or griddle over high heat with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Cook the pork in batches for 3 minutes per side until browned at the edges and cooked through to 145°F (63°C). Do not crowd the pan.
Add the pineapple slices to the pan and sear for 2 minutes until charred, then chop them.
Chop the pork into small pieces and mix with the chopped pineapple.
Warm the tortillas on a dry hot pan for 30 seconds per side.
Fill each tortilla with pork, the remaining diced pineapple, diced onion and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
Put the chicken in a pot with [[2 cups]] of the broth, half the onion and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer covered for 35 minutes until cooked to 165°F (74°C). Remove the chicken and keep the broth.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] lard in a skillet. Toast the chiles for about 20 seconds per side until fragrant, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes.
In the same skillet, fry the almonds, raisins, tortilla, cinnamon, cloves and peppercorns for 3 minutes until toasted, then add the sesame seeds for 30 seconds.
Char the tomatoes, remaining onion and garlic in a dry pan for 8 minutes until browned.
Drain the chiles. Blend them with the toasted mixture, the tomatoes, onion, garlic and [[1 cup]] of the broth until smooth, adding more broth as needed.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] lard in a large pot. Pour in the paste carefully, since it will spatter, and fry for 8 minutes, stirring often.
Add the chocolate, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 cup]] more broth. Simmer on low for 30 minutes, stirring, until dark and thick like gravy.
Add the chicken to the mole and simmer for 10 minutes to warm through. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with rice and tortillas.
Mix the onion, chile, half the cilantro and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl. Mash with a fork to release the flavor.
Cut the avocados in half, remove the pits and scoop the flesh into the bowl.
Add the lime juice, which stops the avocado from browning.
Mash with a fork to the texture you like, leaving it a bit chunky.
Fold in the diced tomato and the rest of the cilantro.
Taste and add more salt or lime. Serve right away with tortilla chips.
Heat the broiler. Place the tomatillos and chiles on a baking sheet.
Broil for 5 minutes until blistered and charred, then flip and broil 4 minutes more.
Let them cool a few minutes, then add everything including any juices to a blender.
Add the garlic, onion, cilantro, lime juice and [[0.75 tsp]] salt.
Blend until mostly smooth, adding water a spoonful at a time to loosen it.
Taste and adjust salt and lime. Serve cold or warm with chips, tacos or enchiladas.

ing: half quartered, half finely diced to serve
st: Put the pork, quartered onion, [[4 cloves]] garlic, [[2 tsp]] salt and the water in a large pot. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Lower the heat, cover partly and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes until the pork is tender.
Soak the chiles in hot water for 15 minutes until soft.
Blend the chiles with the remaining garlic and [[1 cup]] of the cooking broth until smooth. Strain it into the pot.
Add the hominy and oregano. Simmer for 30 minutes more so the flavors blend.
Remove the pork, shred it into bite-size pieces and return it to the pot. Taste and adjust salt.
Ladle into bowls. Top with cabbage, diced onion, radishes and a squeeze of lime.
Char the poblanos under a hot broiler or over a gas flame for 10 minutes, turning, until blackened all over.
Put them in a bowl, cover with a plate and let them steam for 10 minutes, then peel off the skins.
Cut a slit in each pepper, remove the seeds and stuff in a stick of cheese. Dust lightly with flour.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic, broth and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Simmer in a pan for 10 minutes until slightly thick.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks. Fold in the yolks and [[0.5 tsp]] salt gently.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Dip each pepper in flour, then coat in the egg mixture. Fry 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden.
Drain on paper towels. Serve with the warm tomato sauce spooned over.

ing: finely diced, plus extra for topping
st: Soak the chiles in hot water for 15 minutes until soft, then drain.
Blend the chiles with the tomatoes, garlic, broth and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until smooth. Strain.
Simmer the sauce in a saucepan for 10 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Warm the oil in a skillet. Dip each tortilla in the oil for 10 seconds per side to soften, then dip it in the sauce.
Fill each tortilla with chicken, a little cheese and onion, then roll up and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the remaining sauce over the top and cover with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 15 minutes until bubbling. Drizzle with crema and scatter with onion before serving.
Simmer the pork with [[6 cups]] water, [[1 tsp]] salt and half the garlic for 1 hour 15 minutes until very tender. Shred the meat.
Soak the corn husks in hot water for 30 minutes until pliable. Soak the chiles in hot water for 15 minutes.
Blend the chiles with the remaining garlic, cumin and [[1 cup]] of the broth, then cook the sauce 5 minutes with the shredded pork.
Beat the lard with an electric mixer for 3 minutes until fluffy.
Mix the masa harina, baking powder and [[1.5 tsp]] salt. Beat into the lard, alternating with [[2.5 cups]] broth, until it is like thick cake batter.
Spread about [[0.25 cup]] masa over the smooth side of a husk, leaving a border. Spoon pork filling down the middle.
Fold the sides in and then fold up the bottom. Stand the tamales open-end up in a steamer basket.
Steam over simmering water, covered, for 1 hour. Add water as needed.
Rest for 15 minutes before unwrapping. The masa should pull cleanly away from the husk.

ing: thinly sliced, pickled with lime to serve
st: Blend the achiote paste, orange juice, lime juice, garlic, vinegar, oregano, cumin and [[2 tsp]] salt until smooth.
Toss the pork with the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). If using banana leaves, warm them over a flame for a few seconds to soften them.
Line a baking dish with the leaves or foil. Add the pork and marinade and wrap tightly to seal.
Roast for 3 hours until the pork shreds easily with a fork and reaches at least 145°F (63°C).
Meanwhile, slice the onion thin and soak in lime juice and a pinch of salt for 30 minutes to quick-pickle.
Shred the pork in its juices.
Serve on warm tortillas topped with the pickled onion.

ing: cut in wedges, or 6 oz tortilla chips
half roughly chopped, half sliced thin to serve
st: Fry the tortilla wedges in [[0.5 cup]] hot oil in batches for 2 minutes until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towels and salt lightly.
Blend the tomatoes, chiles, garlic, chopped onion, broth and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until smooth.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a wide skillet. Pour in the sauce and simmer for 8 minutes until it thickens a little.
Add the chips to the sauce and toss for 1 minute so they soften slightly but still have some bite.
Fry the eggs in a separate pan in the rest of the oil until the whites are set.
Divide the chilaquiles between plates. Top with the eggs, cheese, crema and sliced onion. Eat right away.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Brush the corn with the melted butter if using.
Grill the corn for 10 to 12 minutes, turning often, until tender with charred spots.
Spread each hot ear with an even coat of mayonnaise.
Roll or sprinkle the corn with the cotija so it sticks all over.
Dust with chile powder and a pinch of salt. Serve with lime wedges to squeeze over.

ing: for rolling, plus 1 tbsp for the dough
st: Bring the water, butter, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and the salt to a rolling boil in a saucepan.
Take the pan off the heat. Add all the flour at once and stir hard until a smooth dough forms.
Return to low heat and stir for 1 minute to dry out the dough, then cool for 5 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time until the dough is smooth and glossy.
Spoon the dough into a piping bag with a large star tip.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] sugar and the cinnamon on a plate.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Pipe 5-inch strips into the oil, cutting with scissors. Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain briefly, then roll in the cinnamon sugar while hot. Serve warm.
Stir [[2.25 tsp]] yeast and [[1 tbsp]] sugar into [[1.5 cup]] warm water (about 105°F). Wait 8 minutes until foamy.
Add [[4 cup]] flour, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[2 tbsp]] lard. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and springy.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 8 pieces. Flatten each, fold into a tight oval, and pinch the seam. Taper both ends to a point.
Place seam down on a floured tray, cover and rise 40 minutes. Heat the oven to 425°F with a pan of hot water on the bottom rack.
Slash each roll lengthwise with a sharp knife. Bake 22 to 25 minutes until golden with a crackly crust.
nt: Baked at 425°F with steam
Best swap: use vegetable shortening or neutral oil in place of lard for the same 2 tbsp.

st: Mix [[3.5 cup]] flour, [[0.25 cup]] sugar, [[2.25 tsp]] yeast, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, orange zest and [[1 tsp]] anise in a bowl.
Add [[0.5 cup]] warm milk, 2 eggs and 1 yolk, then knead for 5 minutes. Work in [[0.5 cup]] soft butter and knead 10 minutes more until silky.
Cover and rise 1.5 hours in a warm place until doubled.
Pinch off one quarter of the dough. Shape the rest into a round loaf on a lined tray. Roll the pinched dough into 3 ropes and 1 small ball.
Lay the ropes over the loaf like bones and press the ball in the center. Rise 45 minutes. Heat the oven to 350°F.
Brush with beaten egg white and bake 30 minutes until golden. Brush with melted butter and roll in [[0.25 cup]] sugar while warm.
nt: Baked at 350°F
Best swap: use 1 tbsp orange blossom water in place of anise for a classic variation.

st: Heat the oven to 350°F. Slice the bread into 1 inch pieces and toast in the oven for 10 minutes until dry and crisp.
Simmer the piloncillo, cinnamon, cloves and [[3 cup]] water for 15 minutes until syrupy, then strain.
Butter a 9 by 13 inch dish and layer half the toasted bread over the base.
Scatter half the raisins, peanuts and queso fresco over the bread, then add the remaining bread and toppings.
Slowly pour the warm syrup over everything so the bread soaks it up evenly. Press down gently with a spatula.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 more minutes until the top is lightly golden.
Rest for 10 minutes and serve warm.
nt: Baked at 350°F
Best swap: use mild cheddar or Monterey Jack in place of queso fresco 1 to 1.

st: Pour [[4 cup]] water into a medium pot with the piloncillo, cinnamon stick and cloves. Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, stirring until the piloncillo dissolves.
Simmer for 3 minutes so the cinnamon and clove flavor the sweet water, which will smell warm and caramelly.
Turn off the heat and stir in [[4 tbsp]] coarse ground coffee. Add the orange peel if using.
Cover the pot and steep for 5 minutes. The coffee will settle and the brew will darken.
Strain through a fine sieve or cloth into mugs, discarding the grounds and spices. Serve hot.
nt: Simmered with spices, then steeped off the heat
Best swap: no piloncillo, use 3 tablespoons dark brown sugar plus 1 teaspoon molasses.

st: Warm the sugar and water in a small pot over medium heat until clear, about 3 minutes, then cool completely.
Blend the mango, lime juice, syrup and salt until perfectly smooth. Taste: it should be a little too sweet because freezing mutes sweetness.
Chill the puree in the fridge for 1 hour.
Churn in an ice cream maker for 25 to 30 minutes until the texture is thick. Traditionally it is churned over salted ice in a wooden barrel.
Transfer to a container and freeze 2 hours until scoopable.
Scoop and sprinkle lightly with chili powder if you like it spicy.
nt: Fruit sorbet, churned
Best swap: use 3 cups frozen mango chunks blended with the syrup for a no-churn version, or use tamarind pulp instead of mango.

st: Wash the mangoes, pineapple, cucumber and watermelon under cold water and dry them. Scrub the rinds well, since the knife will carry anything on the skin inside.
Peel the jicama with a sharp vegetable peeler, taking off the thick brown skin and the fibrous layer under it. Cut it into sticks about 1 cm thick and 8 cm long.
Peel the cucumber in alternating stripes, and cut into sticks of the same size. Slice the watermelon into batons, matching the jicama.
Cut the mango cheeks off both sides of the stone, score each in a 1 cm grid without piercing the skin, then push the skin inward and slice off the cubes or fans.
Peel the pineapple, cut out the eyes, quarter it, trim off the core, and slice into thick spears you can hold in your hand.
Pile everything in a bowl or paper cups. Squeeze the lime juice over the top, about [[3 tbsp]] total, and toss gently so the fruit is coated but not soggy.
Dust with [[2 tbsp]] chile-lime powder and the pinch of salt. Add a drizzle of chamoy if you like it sweeter and sticky. Serve immediately with long skewers.
nt: Don't cook: cut and arrange
Best swap: sliced raw turnip or crisp Asian pear for jicama, and paprika with lime zest and a little salt for chile-lime powder.

ing: bone in, cut in large pieces
st: Toast the chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds per side until fragrant, then soak in hot water 20 minutes until soft.
Blend the drained chiles with the garlic, [[2 tbsp]] vinegar, cumin, oregano, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 cup]] of the soaking water until smooth. Strain it.
Coat the meat in the adobo and marinate in the fridge at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Lay a parchment square flat, add a portion of meat with sauce and an avocado leaf, gather the corners into a pouch and tie tightly with twine.
Set a steamer rack in a large pot with 2 inches of water. Stack the parcels, cover tightly and steam over medium-low heat, topping up water as needed.
Check that the meat is fork tender and reads 180°F. Open the parcels at the table and serve with warm tortillas, onion and lime.
nt: Slow steamed in sealed parcels, not grilled, 2.5 hours
Best swap: bake the sealed parcels in a covered pan at 325°F for 2.5 hours. Use chicken thighs for lamb, and bay leaves for avocado leaves.

st: Peel the brittle shells off the tamarind pods and pull away the long stringy veins. Place the sticky pulp in a bowl.
Pour [[3 cups]] hot water over the pulp and let it soak until very soft and falling apart from the seeds.
Squeeze and mash the pulp with your hands or a spoon to free it from the seeds, then pour everything through a fine strainer into a pitcher, pressing hard on the solids.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] piloncillo until dissolved, then add [[3 cups]] cold water. Taste and add more sugar if it is too sharp.
Chill until cold, stir again because the pulp settles, and pour over ice. Serve with a lime wedge.
nt: Don't cook: soak, mash and strain, serve over ice
Best swap: use 1 cup tamarind paste concentrate (seedless) instead of pods, whisked into 6 cups water, for a 5-minute version.

st: Mix [[3.5 cup]] flour, the warm milk, yeast, [[0.33 cup]] sugar, eggs and a pinch of salt. Knead in [[0.5 cup]] soft butter and work the dough 10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Mash the topping butter, powdered sugar, [[0.5 cup]] flour and vanilla into a soft paste. Split in half and knead cocoa into one half if you like.
Divide the dough into 10 balls and flatten slightly on lined trays. Cover and rest 40 minutes until puffy. Heat the oven to 350°F.
Flatten a golf ball size piece of topping into a thin disc and press it over each bun. Cut shell lines with a knife or concha cutter.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes until the buns sound hollow and the edges are lightly golden.
nt: Baked at 350°F
Best swap: use vegetable shortening in the topping for the classic crisp-soft crust, or vegan butter to avoid dairy.

st: Simmer the tomatoes, jalapeno, garlic and a quarter of the onion in water for 8 minutes until soft. Drain.
Blend the cooked mixture with [[0.5 tsp]] salt until smooth. Cook it in a pan with [[1 tbsp]] oil for 6 minutes until it thickens and darkens. Keep warm.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the tortillas about 30 seconds per side until lightly crisp, drain, and set on two plates.
Spread the warm refried beans over the tortillas.
Fry the eggs in the same skillet with [[1 tbsp]] oil over medium-low heat until the whites are fully set, about 3 minutes. Cover for a minute for firm yolks. Eggs should reach 160°F for safety.
Place two eggs on each plate, spoon the hot sauce over, and top with queso fresco, remaining onion and cilantro.
nt: Boiled and blended sauce, pan-fried eggs
Best swap: use one 14 oz can of fire-roasted tomatoes with a chipotle in adobo instead of fresh tomatoes.

st: Cut the cleaned cactus paddles into 1/2 inch squares. If you buy whole paddles, scrape off the spines and trim the edges first with a knife.
Put the nopales in a pot with water to cover, a pinch of salt and half the onion. Boil for 10 to 12 minutes until tender and olive-green.
Drain and rinse under cold water for a full minute to remove the slime. Drain well and pat dry.
Combine the nopales with the tomatoes, remaining onion, cilantro and jalapeño.
Add [[3 tbsp]] lime juice, [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and salt. Toss, then top with the crumbled cheese and serve at room temperature or chilled.
nt: Boiled paddles, then tossed cold
Best swap: jarred nopalitos, drained and rinsed, 1 lb equivalent, to skip the boiling.

st: Rinse [[1 cup]] rice in a sieve under cold water for 20 seconds. Break the cinnamon stick into a few pieces.
Put rice and cinnamon in a bowl, cover with [[2 cup]] hot (not boiling) water, and soak for at least 4 hours or overnight at room temperature.
Pour everything, soaking water included, into a blender. Blend on high for 2 minutes until the rice is a fine chalky slurry with no big grains.
Set a fine sieve over a pitcher lined with cheesecloth. Pour the mixture through and squeeze the cloth to extract all the liquid. Discard the solids.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] vanilla and [[2 cup]] cold water until the sugar dissolves. Add the milk if you want it richer.
Chill for 30 minutes if you can. Stir well before pouring, because the rice settles, and serve over ice with a dusting of cinnamon.
nt: Soaked overnight, then blended and strained
Best swap: replace the milk with an equal amount of water or almond milk for a dairy-free horchata.

st: Put the chicken, stock, chopped onion, garlic, oregano and salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through to 165°F.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat off the bones, and discard the bones. Strain the broth and return it to the pot.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tortilla strips in batches for 1 to 2 minutes until golden, then drain on paper towels and salt lightly.
In a small pan, soften the sliced onion and tomato in a spoonful of the frying oil for 4 minutes, then add them to the broth.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot and warm through for 5 minutes. Add the lime juice off the heat so it stays fresh and not bitter.
Ladle into bowls, top with fried tortilla strips, the lime slices and cilantro.
nt: Simmered broth with fried tortilla topping
Best swap: use 2 limes plus 1 tbsp orange juice per 3 sweet limes if you cannot find sweet limes.

st: Toss the pork with [[1 tbsp]] salt, oregano and cumin. Leave 30 minutes at room temperature.
In a heavy Dutch oven, melt the lard. Add the pork, onion, garlic, bay and the juice of the orange and limes. Add the squeezed orange halves too.
Add water just until the pork is nearly covered. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook at a gentle bubble for 2 hours.
Uncover and keep simmering 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the liquid evaporates and the pork fries in its own fat.
Raise the heat to medium-high and fry, turning the pieces, for 10 minutes until browned and crisp at the edges. Break up with two forks.
Pile into warm tortillas with cilantro, onion and lime wedges.
nt: Simmered tender, then fried crisp in its own fat
Best swap: finish on a sheet pan under the broiler for 8 minutes instead of frying in the pot. Use oil in place of lard.

st: Rinse [[1 cup]] hibiscus flowers in a strainer under cold water to remove any dust.
Bring [[3 cup]] water and the cinnamon stick to a boil in a pot.
Add the flowers, turn off the heat, cover, and steep for 20 minutes until the water is a deep ruby red.
Strain into a pitcher, pressing the flowers with a spoon, then discard them and the cinnamon.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] sugar while the liquid is still hot so it dissolves.
Add the remaining [[3 cup]] cold water and the juice of 1 lime. Taste; it should be tart and fruity, so add sugar if needed.
Chill for 1 hour and serve over plenty of ice.
nt: Steeped in hot water, then chilled
Best swap: honey or agave in place of the sugar, [[0.33 cup]] stirred in while the tea is hot.

st: Heat [[0.25 cup]] olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the carrots and onion for 5 minutes until the onion softens.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant and lightly golden, without burning.
Add the jalapenos and cook 3 minutes, stirring, until they turn dull olive green.
Pour in [[1.5 cups]] vinegar and [[0.5 cup]] water. Add the bay leaves, oregano, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[2 tsp]] salt. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes, then taste the brine. It should be sharp and slightly salty. Cool to room temperature.
Transfer to a clean jar, seal and refrigerate. Eat after 24 hours, and keep up to 1 month. Wear gloves when slicing the chiles.
nt: Sauteed in oil then simmered in vinegar
Best swap: serrano chiles for jalapenos for more heat; for mild, use banana peppers at the same weight.

st: Rub [[0.5 cup]] butter and the lard into [[3 cup]] flour and [[1 tsp]] salt until crumbly. Add [[0.5 cup]] cold water, press into a dough and chill 30 minutes.
Brown the beef in a skillet over medium-high heat for 6 minutes, breaking it up. It must be cooked through with no pink.
Add the onion, poblano and potato with [[1 tsp]] salt. Cook 10 minutes until the potato is just tender, then cool completely.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Divide the dough into 8 pieces and roll each into a 6 inch circle.
Spoon filling onto half of each circle. Fold over, then crimp the edge into a rope pattern with your fingers to seal.
Brush with beaten egg and bake on a lined tray 30 minutes until deep golden. Serve warm with salsa.
nt: Baked at 375°F
Best swap: use cooked shredded chicken or sliced mushrooms 1 to 1 for the beef; green bell pepper replaces poblano.

ing: pork shoulder, cut in 2 inch cubes
st: Place the pork in a pot, cover with water and add [[1 tsp]] oregano and 2 garlic cloves. Simmer gently for 50 minutes until a cube shreds easily with a fork.
Meanwhile, simmer the tomatoes, chiles de arbol and the last garlic clove in [[2 cup]] water for 12 minutes until the chiles soften and the tomatoes burst.
Blend the tomato mixture with [[2 tbsp]] vinegar and salt until smooth. Strain it for a silky, thin sauce. It should be hot and brick red.
Soak the sliced onion in lime juice with a pinch of salt for 10 minutes so it turns pink and loses its bite.
Drain the pork and shred or chop it. Warm it in a skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes, seasoning with salt.
Split each roll lengthwise, spread with [[0.25 cup]] refried beans, then fill with pork and a spoon of pickled onion.
Set each torta in a shallow bowl and ladle hot sauce over it until soaked. Serve with extra sauce and lime wedges. Eat with a fork or fast with your hands.
nt: Simmered, then sauced, served soaked
Best swap: use crusty French baguette sections for birote. Use 1 cup cooked jackfruit in place of 1.5 lb pork for a vegetarian version.

ing: cod or mahi mahi, cut in strips
or sour cream thinned with lime
st: Whisk the flour, cumin and a pinch of salt with the cold beer into a thin batter, like pancake batter. Rest it 10 minutes.
Stir the crema with half the lime juice and a pinch of salt. Toss the cabbage with the rest of the lime juice and the cilantro.
Heat the oil to 375°F in a heavy pot. Pat the fish dry and salt it lightly.
Dip the strips in the batter and fry in batches for 3 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and the fish reaches 145°F.
Drain on a rack, then pile fish into warm tortillas with cabbage and a spoon of crema. Serve with lime wedges.
nt: Deep fried in a beer batter
Best swap: bake the strips at 450°F for 12 minutes on a rack after coating in panko, or use gluten-free flour 1 to 1.

st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 4 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and poblano and cook 2 minutes.
Add the zucchini and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cook 6 minutes, stirring, until just tender with some color.
Stir in the corn and tomato. Cook 5 minutes until the tomato softens and the corn is hot.
Remove from the heat, top with the crumbled queso fresco and let it soften for 1 minute before serving.
nt: Sauteed in a skillet
Best swap: use crumbled feta in place of the queso fresco at the same amount, or skip the cheese for a vegan version.
